source_snapshot.procedure: Set full-population fan duty to 25/50/75/100% with OEM raw 0x30/0x21, read SDR and raw 0x30/0x22, restore auto; then set 75%, physically remove/reinstall one fan, re-read and restore auto.
source_snapshot.criteria: Manual duty succeeds with correct readings, auto control restores, and the reinstalled fan retains the manual setting.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; 10 attended and 10 machine minutes; duplicate code exists in another workbook row.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Its OEM bytes conflict with the source, it does not execute or govern the required fan removal/reinstall, and its stated evidence does not measure fan response.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly rejects all unresolved raw forms, preserves the staged duty and physical objectives, and adds independent thermal recovery controls.
historical_reviews.history: The same code has a later distinct source-row variant; identity is therefore sheet/row/hash/variant, not code alone.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Manual PWM overrides the controller's thermal policy, while physical fan removal reduces cooling capacity at the same time. The second phase is not a simple repeat: the expected retained 75% behavior must be defined for the removed slot and surviving fans, and auto restore must be independently proven even after abort.

original_test_intent: Verify documented manual fan-duty control across approved duty points, verify correct controller/readback and actual RPM response, test one approved fan removal/reinstallation under manual control, then restore automatic cooling safely.
original_method: Vendor-validate exact set/read/auto commands and duty matrix; capture full fan/thermal baseline; with per-phase approval set one duty at a time under bounded dwell and independent watchdog, compare commanded PWM to per-fan RPM; restore auto; only under a supported physical procedure set the approved duty, remove/reinstall the identified fan, verify detection and response, and unconditionally restore and prove automatic control.
manual_activity: The owner/FAE validates commands, duties, limits and hot-plug support; an operator approves each override and physically removes/reinstalls the named fan under the approved procedure while monitoring the independent abort path.
required_inputs: Vendor 0x30/0x21 and 0x30/0x22 contract or approved replacement
Approved duty points and RPM tolerances
Independent monitoring and emergency max-fan path
safety_requirements: Never run conflicting or undocumented OEM bytes
Approve each duty and physical phase
Use bounded dwell with independent temperature/RPM watchdog
Abort on stall, stale telemetry, thermal rise or BMC loss
Do not remove an unidentified or unsupported fan
Keep hands clear of rotating parts and follow ESD policy
Unconditionally restore auto after success or failure
Never clear logs or automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify commands, fan map and cooling baseline
Coordinate per-duty writes and complete telemetry
Enforce abort and unconditional auto restore
Coordinate but not perform the physical action
Verify removal/reinsert detection and retained-mode semantics
Prove final auto cooling and archive evidence
engineer_actions: Approve vendor raw contract, duty matrix and safe limits
Approve dedicated target and each phase
Perform or supervise the physical fan action

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's 0x30/0x31 set and 0x30/0x81 restore do not match the source 0x30/0x21 contract, omit the required physical phase and cite unrelated temperature sensors.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the firmware-approved manual-duty/readback/auto-restore sequence, one approved duty at a time under watchdog; execute the 75%-plus-reinstall phase only with the owner-approved physical procedure.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 25/50/75/100% sequence, available PWM mapping, 75% reinstall phase and 10/10-minute estimate are preserved, but none is executable until command and safety contracts are proven.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain a per-phase ledger of command bytes, requested duty, all fan RPM/PWM, temperatures, alarms, dwell/abort result, target-fan presence transition, survivor behavior and final auto-control proof.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds command provenance, independent interlocks, physical safety and unconditional rollback around each state change.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Command success and one grepped fan line cannot prove proportional response across all fans, safe thermals, reinsertion behavior or restored control ownership.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RPM is not necessarily linear with PWM, and controller policy may override unsafe duties. Acceptance needs vendor tolerances rather than exact percentage equality.

project_override_considerations: The Project must resolve exact OEM bytes, whether the mapping list is informational or adds required 20/70/90% points, and the expected 75% behavior for the removed/reinserted fan and surviving fans. The later duplicate-code row is a separate variant and must not be merged by code.
expected_evidence: Per-phase approval, target identity, vendor raw contract, duty/tolerance and safety limits
Baseline and timestamped complete fan RPM/PWM/temperature/alarm data
Each set/read response and bounded dwell/abort decision
Named fan removal/reinsert physical record and presence/response timeline
Unconditional auto-restore readback and final stable cooling health
Preserved SEL/OS/BMC logs, no-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets manual duty, readback, physical reinstall behavior and auto restore. The additional PWM values can be treated as a mapping until the Project declares them required; DeepSeek's conflicting bytes are a reference error, not competing Master intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor raw semantics, safety limits and the fan service procedure are obtainable project inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if auto restore, independent monitoring or safe physical handling cannot be proven.

review_improvement: Prevents mismatched OEM commands and unrelated evidence from controlling cooling, while preserving the distinct physical reinstall objective and enforcing a verifiable automatic-mode recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: A reported manual-mode bit does not prove that every fan followed the requested duty, and fan inertia plus sampling intervals can hide a stalled or lagging rotor. During removal, the controller may boost survivors or abandon the manual setpoint; that may be correct safety behavior. Therefore the oracle must distinguish target-slot absence, survivor response, reinserted-fan recovery and final control ownership rather than demand a simplistic instantaneous RPM percentage.
